description: Spec-derived test vectors for draft-hardt-httpbis-signature-key. Every vector publishes the RFC 9421 signature base verbatim.
source_of_truth: the draft text, not an implementation

field_notes.key: the key the vector's scheme member resolves to. On a positive vector it is also the signing key. Absent from a negative whose fault is that the member resolves to nothing usable.
field_notes.keys: per-label key material, present only where labels resolve to different keys.
field_notes.signing_key: the key that actually produced the Signature header. On a negative this is deliberately not the key the header names: the signature is sound so that an end-to-end verifier reaches the rule under test instead of stopping at invalid_signature.
field_notes.unsigned: true on the two vectors that cannot carry a signature at all, with unsigned_reason giving the reason.
field_notes.signature_base_is_informational: the request is signed and the base is real, but a conforming verifier rejects on the assertion's claims before it needs the base, so do not treat the base as the thing under test.
field_notes.applies_to: a precondition on the verifier, not on the request. verifier_bounds_iat means the vector is a must-reject only for a verifier that bounds iat.

positive_vectors.name: hwk-okp-ed25519
positive_vectors.notes: Inline OKP key. No kid, forbidden by the hwk scheme: the key is carried inline so there is nothing for an identifier to select. Ed25519 is deterministic (RFC 8032), so the Signature value reproduces byte for byte.

positive_vectors.name: hwk-ec-p256
positive_vectors.notes: Inline EC key. ECDSA is randomised, so the Signature value here is ONE valid signature, not the only one. Compare the signature base, then verify the signature; do not compare signature bytes.

positive_vectors.name: jkt-jwt-enclave-p256-delegates-ed25519
positive_vectors.notes: Enclave P-256 identity key delegates to an Ed25519 ephemeral request key via cnf.jwk. iss is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the HEADER jwk, prefixed per the typ. The HTTP signature is made by the cnf.jwk key, not the enclave key. The delegation JWT itself is ECDSA and so not reproducible; the HTTP signature is Ed25519 and is.

positive_vectors.name: jwks_uri-discovery-ed25519
positive_vectors.notes: Two-hop discovery. The metadata document MUST carry issuer, and issuer MUST equal the id parameter by byte equality as presented. The alg travels only on the resolved JWKS entry, because the header conveys id, dwk and kid, which identify a key rather than describe it.

positive_vectors.name: jwks-direct-ed25519
positive_vectors.notes: One hop, no metadata document. The URL is both identifier and key location, compared by byte equality and never canonicalised, so any byte difference names a different signer.

positive_vectors.name: jwt-cnf-ed25519
positive_vectors.notes: Issuer-minted assertion carrying the request key in cnf.jwk. exp is MUST, it is what bounds how long the confirmation key is accepted. No cache parameter, so no jti is required here.

positive_vectors.name: jwt-cnf-ed25519-cache-requested
positive_vectors.notes: Same as jwt-cnf-ed25519 plus the cache parameter. Boolean true is serialised by omitting the value per RFC 9651 4.1.1.2, so it appears as 'cache' and not 'cache=?1'. A JWT presented with cache MUST carry jti; a verifier MUST NOT issue a cache identifier for one without it. The parameter sits inside the covered signature-key component, so the request signature covers the cache request itself.

positive_vectors.name: self-jwt-es256
positive_vectors.notes: Issuer and signer are the same party, so one key verifies both the JWT and the HTTP message signature. cnf MUST be absent, and a verifier MUST reject a self-jwt that carries one. No cache parameter is supported for this scheme. Both signatures are ECDSA, so neither reproduces byte for byte; compare the base and verify.

positive_vectors.name: multi-signature-hwk-and-jwks
positive_vectors.notes: Both labels cover signature-key, and the COMPLETE Signature-Key header was populated before either signature was made, so each signature protects both members' key material. Both labels therefore share one identical signature base. The two members resolve to DIFFERENT keys, so the two signatures over that one base differ, which is what makes the vector able to catch a verifier that resolves one label and reuses its key for the other. Each member is resolved independently: sig1 from the inline hwk key, sig2 from its own url and kid. Label correlation is by equality of label name across Signature-Input, Signature and Signature-Key. Per-label key material is under keys; key repeats sig1 for harnesses that expect a single key.

positive_vectors.name: mldsa-44-verify-only
positive_vectors.notes: Verify-only, category 2. ML-DSA sits here on exactly the same footing as ECDSA and RSA-PSS: FIPS 204 specifies the hedged variant as the default, so a second run produces a different signature. Signature is 2420 bytes. Verification is deterministic, so any implementation supporting the algorithm gets a definite answer from this vector. ML-DSA-44 key, 1312 byte public value per FIPS 204, carried as the AKP key type of RFC 9964 with the algorithm named by alg rather than derivable from the key structure.

positive_vectors.name: mldsa-44-deterministic-optional
positive_vectors.notes: The same base as mldsa-44-verify-only, signed with the deterministic variant of FIPS 204, where rnd is all zeros. The hedged variant degrades to exactly this when the RBG returns zeros, so an implementation that can inject rnd reproduces these bytes. Most libraries do not expose that knob, so this vector is OPTIONAL and MUST NOT be required to pass. It is published because for the implementations that can reach it, it is the only ML-DSA vector that tests a SIGNER rather than a verifier. ML-DSA-44 key, 1312 byte public value per FIPS 204, carried as the AKP key type of RFC 9964 with the algorithm named by alg rather than derivable from the key structure.

negative_vectors.name: hwk-with-kid-forbidden
negative_vectors.rule: The kid parameter MUST NOT be used with hwk. The key is carried inline, so there is nothing for an identifier to select, and a kid that disagrees with the inline key has no defined resolution. This is a member the document forbids: understood and rejected, not unknown and ignored.

negative_vectors.name: hwk-alg-absent
negative_vectors.rule: A verifier MUST reject a JWK whose alg member is absent, and MUST NOT select an algorithm for it by inspecting other key parameters. kty and crv would determine it here; the draft requires alg regardless.

negative_vectors.name: hwk-alg-polymorphic-eddsa
negative_vectors.rule: The polymorphic EdDSA identifier MUST NOT be used. Use the fully-specified Ed25519 or Ed448 identifiers of RFC 9864.

negative_vectors.name: hwk-alg-kty-inconsistent
negative_vectors.rule: A verifier MUST verify kty and, where present, crv are consistent with alg, and MUST reject the key if they are not. alg ES256 with kty RSA is inconsistent. Rejecting on disagreement stops a key being used under either of two conflicting interpretations.

negative_vectors.name: hwk-alg-crv-inconsistent
negative_vectors.rule: Same rule on the curve: alg ES256 with crv P-384 is inconsistent and MUST be rejected.

negative_vectors.name: hwk-symmetric-forbidden
negative_vectors.rule: Symmetric algorithms MUST NOT be used. The oct key type and the JOSE MAC identifiers name a shared secret rather than a public key, and a verifier MUST reject a scheme that conveys or references such a key.
negative_vectors.unsigned_reason: kty is oct. The scheme defines no symmetric mode, so there is no signing procedure for the key this member declares. Signing with an unrelated asymmetric key would add a second fault and make the vector test the wrong thing.

negative_vectors.name: unknown-scheme-selected
negative_vectors.rule: A verifier that selects a member whose scheme token it does not implement, including any unregistered value, MUST reject with unsupported_scheme and MUST NOT fail in a scheme-specific or undefined manner. Dispatch SHOULD be a registry lookup, not a fixed set of branches.
negative_vectors.unsigned_reason: the selected scheme is unknown by construction, so no signing procedure is defined for it. A signature made under some other scheme is not the thing the verifier is asked to reject.

negative_vectors.name: self-jwt-with-cnf-forbidden
negative_vectors.rule: Verifiers MUST validate that cnf is absent before treating the scheme as self-issued; a JWT containing cnf MUST be rejected. A self-jwt's signing key IS its confirmation key, so a cnf claim is a different trust model wearing this scheme's name.

negative_vectors.name: jwks_uri-issuer-mismatch
negative_vectors.rule: The metadata document's issuer MUST equal the id parameter by byte equality as presented. Without the check, a document served under id through shared hosting or subdomain takeover could point jwks_uri at keys that do not belong to id, and the verifier would attribute the request accordingly.

negative_vectors.name: jwks_uri-issuer-missing
negative_vectors.rule: The document MUST contain issuer and jwks_uri. Reject with issuer_missing if issuer is absent.

negative_vectors.name: label-missing-from-signature-key
negative_vectors.rule: If the Signature-Key header is present and the verifier is attempting to verify a label using it, but the corresponding dictionary member is missing, verification for that signature MUST fail. Here the verifier wants label 'sig' and Signature-Key carries only 'other'.

negative_vectors.name: unselected-member-unknown-scheme-MUST-ACCEPT
negative_vectors.rule: A verifier MUST NOT reject a request because a member it did not select names a scheme the verifier does not implement. This is the companion to unsupported_scheme and the one a naive implementation fails: without it no signer could offer a new scheme without breaking every verifier that lacks it, so none would, and the registry would have no path into deployment. Verify label 'sig' and ignore 'future'.
negative_vectors.draft_section: Signature-Key Header / Unknown schemes + Label Consistency

negative_vectors.name: akp-only-jwks-must-decline-not-throw
negative_vectors.rule: A verifier that encounters a JWK whose kty it does not implement, including the AKP key type, MUST reject the key with defined error feedback and MUST NOT fail in an undefined manner. Absence of support for a key type is a reason to decline, not a parsing failure. An implementation without ML-DSA must report unsupported_algorithm here rather than throw. ML-DSA-44 key, 1312 byte public value per FIPS 204, carried as the AKP key type of RFC 9964 with the algorithm named by alg rather than derivable from the key structure.

negative_vectors.name: mixed-jwks-ignore-unparseable-neighbour-MUST-ACCEPT
negative_vectors.rule: The JWKS holds an Ed25519 key and an ML-DSA-44 key, and the vector selects the Ed25519 one by kid. A verifier MUST select the member matching kid without requiring any other member to be usable, and MUST NOT fail because an unselected member names a kty or alg it does not implement. The failure mode is a library that hits the unknown kty while enumerating and abandons a perfectly good key sitting next to it. Exercising the unknown-value path routinely is what stops it rotting, in the spirit of RFC 9170. ML-DSA-44 key, 1312 byte public value per FIPS 204, carried as the AKP key type of RFC 9964 with the algorithm named by alg rather than derivable from the key structure.

negative_vectors.name: signature-key-not-covered
negative_vectors.rule: Every signature MUST cover the signature-key component, so that the signature protects the key material that verifies it. Here the signer covered the first three and left signature-key out, which leaves the key material unprotected and swappable. The server SHOULD answer invalid_input with a required_input member naming the components it requires, and MAY omit that member where enumerating its requirements to an unauthenticated caller is a disclosure risk.

negative_vectors.name: jwks-kid-not-in-jwks
negative_vectors.rule: The kid selects no member of the fetched JWKS. The verifier rejects with unknown_key rather than falling back to another member: a JWKS with one usable key is not licence to use it for a kid that does not name it. The server SHOULD re-fetch the JWKS once before answering, to handle a key that rotated between the signer publishing and the verifier reading.

negative_vectors.name: jwt-without-exp
negative_vectors.rule: The jwt scheme requires exp. The assertion carries a confirmation key, and exp is what bounds how long that key is accepted; without it the key remains acceptable indefinitely. A missing required claim is rejected before any signature work.

negative_vectors.name: jwt-expired-one-second-before-now
negative_vectors.rule: exp is now - 1, so the assertion expired one second before the instant this vector declares. Expiry is validated before the signature, so a verifier fails here without cryptographic work. Expressed relative to now (1791275958) rather than as a fixed past date, so the vector does not go stale.

negative_vectors.name: jwt-exp-300s-after-now-MUST-ACCEPT
negative_vectors.rule: exp is now + 300, so the assertion is live at the declared instant and MUST be accepted. This is the positive control for the expiry pair: without it a verifier that rejects every assertion passes the expired case for the wrong reason.

negative_vectors.name: jwt-iat-one-hour-after-now-is-clock-skew
negative_vectors.conditional: 5.4.14 does not require a verifier to bound iat. This vector applies only to a verifier that does. One that does not bound iat is conformant and MUST NOT be failed for accepting this request; it should skip the vector rather than record a miss.
negative_vectors.rule: iat is now + 3600, further ahead of the verifier's clock than any reasonable validity window. The distinct code is what the caller needs: nothing about the assertion or the signature is wrong, the issuer's clock disagrees, and a fresh assertion from the same issuer carries the same skew. A future iat becomes acceptable with time, so the sender MAY wait and present the same assertion again. This is why clock_skew is not invalid_jwt or expired_jwt.
